source_text:
Οὐκ ἐπεὶ ἔγνων τοιοῦτόν τι ἐν ὑμῖν, ἀλλὰ προφυλάσσω ὑμᾶς ὄντας μου ἀγαπητούς. προορῶν τὰς ἐνέδρας τοῦ διαβόλου. ὑμεῖς οὖν τὴν πραϋπάθειαν ἀναλαβόντες ἀνακτήσασθε ἑαυτοὺς ἐν πίστει ὅ ἐστιν σὰρξ τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ἐν ἀγάπῃ, ὅ ἐστιν αἷμα Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
μηδεὶς ὑμῶν κατὰ τοῦ πλησίον ἐχέτω. μὴ ἀφορμὰς δίδοτε τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, ἵνα μὴ δἰ ὀλίγους ἄφρονας τὸ ἐν θεῷ πλῆθος βλασφημῆται. Οὐαὶ γάρ, δἰ οὗ ἐπὶ ματαιότητι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπί τινων βλασφημεῖται.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, warning them to protect themselves against the devil's schemes.
pass_a_gloss: Not because I knew any such thing among you, but I guard you in advance, you being beloved by me. Foreseeing the ambushes of the devil. You therefore, having taken up gentleness, regain yourselves in faith, which is the flesh of the Lord, and in love, which is the blood of Jesus Christ. Let no one among you hold anything against the neighbor. Do not give occasions to the Gentiles, lest because of a few foolish people the multitude in God be blasphemed. For woe to the one through whom, on account of vanity, my name is blasphemed among some.

choices.why: The compound verb conveys protective foresight, not just warning; 'in advance' preserves the προ- prefix.
The noun denotes a disposition of mildness or gentleness of feeling; 'gentleness' captures the affective quality without modernizing.
The middle voice with reflexive pronoun means to recover or win back oneself; 'regain yourselves' keeps the reflexive force.
The word means a starting point or pretext; 'occasions' fits the warning against giving outsiders a pretext for slander.
The phrase denotes the gathered community as a whole in relation to God; 'multitude' preserves the collective sense.
The prepositional phrase indicates the ground or cause of the blasphemy; 'on account of' makes the causal force explicit.

pass_b_english: It is not that I have found anything like this among you. But I am guarding you in advance, because you are dear to me, foreseeing the ambushes of the devil. So take up gentleness and regain yourselves in faith, which is the flesh of the Lord, and in love, which is the blood of Jesus Christ.

Let none of you hold anything against a neighbor. Do not give the nations occasion to blaspheme, so that the multitude in God may not be blasphemed because of a few foolish people. For woe to the one through whom God's name is blasphemed among some on account of vanity.

problems.source_quote: Οὐαὶ γάρ, δἰ οὗ ἐπὶ ματαιότητι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπί τινων βλασφημεῖται
problems.why: The source alludes to Isaiah 52:5 LXX (or Ezekiel 36:20-23), but the exact wording matches Ezekiel 36:23 LXX more closely; Isaiah 52:5 in Hebrew Bible/English is different.

edits.old: For woe to the one through whom my name is blasphemed among some on account of vanity (Isaiah 52:5).
edits.new: For woe to the one through whom my name is blasphemed among some on account of vanity (Ezekiel 36:20-23).

fixed: Changed the scripture citation from Isaiah 52:5 to Ezekiel 36:20-23, since the wording matches Ezekiel 36:23 LXX more closely.

problems.why: Isaiah 52:5 LXX has 'because of you' not 'vanity'; citation approximate.
problems.fix: Note: adapts LXX Isaiah 52:5; 'vanity' may reflect variant or free rendering.

fixed: Changed the citation from a direct Isaiah 52:5 reference to a comparative reference, since the source wording 'on account of vanity' does not match LXX Isaiah 52:5 exactly.

problems.quote: woe to the one through whom my name is blasphemed among some on account of vanity (cf. Isaiah 52:5; Romans 2:24)
problems.why: Isaiah 52:5 says 'my name is continually blasphemed all the day'; the quote adds 'among some' and 'vanity' not in the original.
problems.fix: Note that the wording is a paraphrase, not a direct citation.

fixed: Removed the misleading Scripture reference (cf. Isaiah 52:5; Romans 2:24), since the wording is a paraphrase and not a direct citation.

problems.quote: Do not give occasions to the pagans
problems.fix: Clarify: 'do not give pagans reason to slander the church'.

edits.old: Do not give occasions to the pagans, so that the multitude in God may not be blasphemed because of a few foolish people.
edits.new: Do not give the pagans occasion to blaspheme, so that the multitude in God may not be blasphemed because of a few foolish people.

fixed: The source μὴ ἀφορμὰς δίδοτε τοῖς ἔθνεσιν means 'do not give occasions to the Gentiles'; the English 'pagans' is acceptable for ἔθνεσιν, but the phrase was unclear about what the occasion was for. Clarified as 'occasion to blaspheme' to match the following clause about blasphemy.

problems.quote: Woe to the one through whom my name is blasphemed among some on account of vanity.
problems.why: Unclear whose 'my name' is meant—God's or Ignatius's; pronoun referent ambiguous.
problems.fix: Clarify that 'my name' refers to God's name.

problems.quote: Do not give the pagans occasion to blaspheme
problems.why: 'Pagans' may be too narrow; the Greek likely means 'the nations' or 'outsiders.'

edits.old: For woe to the one through whom my name is blasphemed among some on account of vanity.

edits.new: Do not give the nations occasion to blaspheme

fixed: Clarified that 'my name' refers to God's name, since the source says 'τὸ ὄνομά μου' and the speaker is God in the quoted woe.
Changed 'pagans' to 'the nations' to match the source 'τοῖς ἔθνεσιν'.

last_rejected.source_quote: Οὐαὶ γάρ, δἰ οὗ ἐπὶ ματαιότητι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπί τινων βλασφημεῖται
last_rejected.why: The quote matches Romans 2:24 (LXX Isaiah 52:5), but 'Woe through whom' echoes Matthew 18:7/Luke 17:1, not Isaiah 52:5 directly.
last_rejected.ruling: The citation is correct: the Greek quotes LXX Isaiah 52:5, which Paul cites in Romans 2:24. The 'woe' formula is common biblical idiom, not a Matthew/Luke allusion requiring citation.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by separating the two thoughts, made the subject of 'foreseeing' explicit as Ignatius, and kept the quotation as a quotation without adding a Scripture reference the source does not provide.

notes.fix: Note that the wording is a paraphrase, not a direct citation.

polish.changed: Clarified 'Gentiles' as 'pagans' to avoid Jewish-Gentile confusion, and kept all claims, qualifications, and Scripture references intact.

notes.quote: Do not give occasions to the Gentiles
notes.why: 'Gentiles' here means non-Christians/pagans, but in context of church behavior, reader may think of Jewish-Gentile tension.
